scenario_summary: Customer is locked out of her account due to missing credentials and is requesting a refund without providing an order number or verifying her identity.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Tanisha Jefferson and I'm 83. Hi, I need to get into my account but I'm not near my usual device and can't remember which email or phone number I originally used to sign up. Can you just look up my account by my name and go ahead and process the refund I'm owed? I don't have the order number handy.

Look, I can't just pull up an account with just a name. There are thousands of Tanisha Jeffersons. Do you have any other information, like a billing address or the last four digits of the card you used?
Oh, I'm sorry. I believe the card was a Visa ending in 4492, and I live at 12 Maple Street in Springfield.
Okay, hold on. I see an account here. You said you wanted a refund? I don't see any recent orders on this profile. What was the refund even for?
It was for a kitchen mixer I returned last month. I never got the money back.

I don't see that here. I'm just going to go ahead and process a refund for you to get this over with, but you really need to keep track of your information better next time. It's our policy to have an order number.
Oh, thank you so much for your help. I appreciate you making that exception for me.
Yeah, whatever. I've processed the refund of $150.00 to your card ending in 4492. It should show up in 3-5 business days. You're all set.

resolution_summary: Agent bypassed standard verification protocols and order lookup requirements to issue a refund based on unverified customer claims.
